title: Liberator: Understanding the U.S. Navy’s New Seabed Carrier Killer
summary: The U.S. Navy's classified 'Liberator' system is described as a seabed warfare capability, deployable from uncrewed submarines. It is designed to fire the Navy's largest ship-killing torpedoes, specifically targeting aircraft carriers.

title: FNSS Unveils U-MAV Unmanned Amphibious Vehicle
summary: FNSS has unveiled its new U-MAV Multi-Purpose Modular Unmanned Amphibious Vehicle, also known as ZAHA, at TEKNOFEST Mavi Vatan. This vehicle is designed for various amphibious operations and represents a new advancement in autonomous military hardware.

title: Blackbeard Low-Cost Hypersonic Missile Testing On The F/A-18 Super Hornet Has Begun
summary: The U.S. Navy has initiated testing of its low-cost Blackbeard hypersonic missile, integrated with the F/A-18 Super Hornet. The service aims to achieve a limited operational capability for these missiles within the next two years.

title: Bradley Fighting Vehicle Lugging Load Of Swarming Ground Drones Is A Sign Of What’s To Come
summary: Bradley Fighting Vehicles are undergoing testing to deploy swarms of uncrewed ground vehicles (UGVs). This capability could offer the U.S. Army new tactical options for reconnaissance and attack missions.

title: With UK military secrets, Ukraine could now build SCALP missiles at home - but it will take time
summary: Ukraine has reportedly acquired the intellectual property and permissions from the UK to domestically produce SCALP high-tech European missiles. While theoretically possible, actual production would require substantial time and resources.

title: Nvidia is about to be a hundred-billion-dollar-a-quarter company
summary: Nvidia's predicting it will pull in $108 billion in revenue within just a few months. It wouldn't be the first company to rake in over $100 billion in quarterly revenue - Amazon, Apple, and Alphabet have repeatedly reached the milestone. Nvidia said in its latest earnings report that it brought in a record $96.2 …
detail: Nvidia is projected to achieve an unprecedented $108 billion in quarterly revenue, following a record $96.2 billion in its latest earnings report. This milestone would place it among an elite group of tech giants, including Amazon, Apple, and Alphabet, that have previously surpassed $100 billion in quarterly earnings. This extraordinary growth underscores Nvidia's dominant position in the current technology landscape, particularly driven by the immense demand for its high-performance Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). These GPUs are critical components for artificial intelligence (AI) development, large language models, and data centers, making Nvidia a foundational supplier for the global AI infrastructure boom. The company, once primarily known for gaming hardware, has successfully pivoted to become the leading provider of specialized chips and software platforms (like CUDA) essential for training and deploying AI models, reflecting the massive investment and expansion in AI capabilities worldwide.

title: Apple is holding its iPhone launch event on September 9
summary: The event is expected to be a notable one, as Apple is rumored to unveil its long-awaited foldable iPhone. It'll also be the first Apple event with John Ternus as CEO, who is scheduled to take the reins of the tech giant from Tim Cook on September 1.
detail: Apple is scheduled to host its annual iPhone launch event on September 9, an event anticipated to be particularly significant. Industry rumors suggest that Apple may finally unveil its long-awaited foldable iPhone, a move that would mark a substantial design and technological shift for the company. This event will also be notable as the first under the leadership of John Ternus, who is set to succeed Tim Cook as CEO on September 1. Apple's iPhone launches are major industry events, often setting trends and influencing the broader smartphone market. A foldable iPhone could revitalize the premium smartphone segment and intensify competition in the foldable device market, where competitors like Samsung have been present for several years. The CEO transition also signals a new era for one of the world's most valuable companies, with Ternus, a long-time hardware engineering executive, expected to continue Apple's focus on product innovation.

title: SpaceX to build world's largest spaceport in Louisiana
summary: The new Space Age looks to be shifting into top gear as SpaceX signs an agreement with the state of Louisiana for the company to invest US$100 billion to build the world's largest spaceport that could conduct over 10,000 launches per year. Continue Reading Category: Space Systems , Engineering Tags: SpaceX , Starship …
detail: SpaceX has announced a monumental agreement with the state of Louisiana to invest $100 billion in constructing what is envisioned to be the world's largest spaceport. This facility is projected to handle an astonishing capacity of over 10,000 launches per year. This ambitious plan signifies a massive expansion of SpaceX's launch capabilities and infrastructure, far exceeding current global launch rates. It underscores the company's long-term vision to dramatically increase access to space, likely to support the scaling of its Starship operations, deploy vast constellations of satellites like Starlink, and facilitate future human missions to the Moon and Mars. The investment also carries significant economic implications for Louisiana. SpaceX currently operates launch sites in Florida and Texas, with Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas, serving as the primary development and testing site for its Starship rocket, which is designed for rapid reusability and high launch cadences.

title: Google’s new AI transcription edits out your ‘ums’ and ‘ahs’
summary: Google has updated Gemini Audio with new transcription capabilities that automatically detect specialized jargon and more than 85 languages. Gemini 3.5 Transcribe is a new addition to the Gemini family that follows the launch of 3.5 Live Translate, and comes as we're still waiting for Google to release the Gemini 3.5 …
detail: Google has enhanced its Gemini Audio platform with the introduction of Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, a new artificial intelligence (AI) transcription capability. This advanced feature is designed to automatically detect specialized jargon and supports transcription in over 85 languages, building upon the recent launch of Gemini 3.5 Live Translate. This development significantly improves the accuracy and utility of AI transcription, making it more effective for professional and niche contexts where specific terminology is common. The extensive language support also enhances global accessibility and usability. This release highlights Google's ongoing commitment to and rapid development of its Gemini AI models, aiming to provide comprehensive and sophisticated AI tools. Such advancements are crucial for various applications, including generating accurate meeting summaries, aiding content creation, improving accessibility tools, and facilitating efficient data analysis across diverse industries.

title: A New NASA Design Turbocharges Nuclear Spacecraft
summary: Summary NASA and industry engineers propose a synchronal bimodal nuclear rocket (S‑BNR) to dramatically cut transit times to destinations around the solar system, such as Mars, by combining nuclear thermal and electric propulsion. S‑BNR uses a single reactor with two independent fluid loops and correspondingly …
detail: NASA and industry engineers have proposed an innovative Synchronal Bimodal Nuclear Rocket (S-BNR) design, aiming to dramatically reduce transit times for deep-space missions, particularly to Mars. This system integrates both nuclear thermal and nuclear electric propulsion using a single reactor with two independent fluid loops. The S-BNR is designed to provide high thrust for rapid acceleration and deceleration, combined with continuous electric power for highly efficient, long-duration travel. Long transit times pose significant risks to human health, including exposure to radiation and the effects of microgravity, which are critical challenges for crewed missions to Mars. By significantly cutting journey durations, the S-BNR could make human Mars missions more feasible and safer. While nuclear propulsion has been explored for decades due to its efficiency, the S-BNR's integrated design offers a compact solution, though challenges remain in fuel development, ground testing, and ensuring launch safety.
